subject: Hosted API pricing: monthly envelope & 99th pct peak TPS (Sparkline)
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Dobson <alex.dobson@sparkline.ai>
Cc: k58rthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-05-03T14:08:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted API pricing: monthly envelope & 99th pct peak TPS (Sparkline)

Alex — thanks for a productive call earlier. Quick recap and explicit asks so we have alignment on pricing and next steps.

Summary of your traffic profile (please confirm):
- Typical sustained: ~7 TPS avg (user-facing inference, 95% of time)
- Peak (99th pct / short bursts): ~170-200 TPS for 20-45 minute windows during product events
- Estimated monthly tokens: 180M - 260M tokens (we heard ~220M as a mid-point)
- Desired unit economics: target $/1M tokens roughly $18-$22 (open to commitments)

What Redwood needs to propose:
1) Hosted API pricing bands (month-to-month vs 12mo commit) with explicit burst policy and burst pricing.
2) Confirmation of acceptable 99th-pct SLO and how fallback to smaller model family will affect latency/quality and unit price.
3) Pilot plan: 30-day pilot scope, keys, and sample traffic file from you so we can size batching/caching.

Immediate asks for you (can reply inline):
- Please confirm the monthly token mid-point we should use for a first-pass quote (we have 220M as working number).
- Share a small traffic sample (JSON/CSV) with per-minute TPS and token-per-request distribution — makes pricing + concurrency recommendations much more accurate.

Next steps we propose:
- Redwood to send 2 pricing options tomorrow: (A) no-commit hosted tier with burst buckets, (B) 12-mo commit with lower $/1M and guaranteed burst capacity.
- 30-min follow-up to review the attached sample pricing matrix and agree on the PO path (billing contacts: procurement@sparkline.ai).

Attachments: we will attach a pricing primer (redwood_pricing_options.pdf) and ask you to attach the sample traffic CSV.

Thanks — Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Alex Dobson <alex.dobson@sparkline.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: k58rthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-05-03T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing: monthly envelope & 99th pct peak TPS (Sparkline)

Thanks Mateo — good summary. Couple clarifications and I attached a tiny sample (sparkline_week1_traffic.csv) showing per-minute TPS for a week. Topline corrections:
- We expect monthly tokens closer to 240M in steady-state if retention/feature rollout goes as planned (so 220M is conservative).
- Peak windows are usually 30 minutes; 99th hits ~185 TPS (we've seen up to 210 in extreme test).
- Quality vs cost: product wants us to keep the main LLM for user-facing responses; fallback to smaller models is OK for non-core summaries but not for primary chat replies.

Target price of $20/1M tokens is our internal target for the first year. Procurement will push for lower on 12-mo commit.

Questions for Redwood:
- If we commit to 12 months at 240M/mo, what is your recommended $/1M and guaranteed 99th capacity?
- During bursts, can Redwood automatically route to a compatible quantized variant to preserve latency while lowering cost?

I'll loop procurement once we have a draft pricing band.

— Alex
Alex Dobson
VP Product, Sparkline AI
alex.dobson@sparkline.ai

Attachment: sparkline_week1_traffic.csv (per-minute TPS sample)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Dobson <alex.dobson@sparkline.ai>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-05-03T18:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing: monthly envelope & 99th pct peak TPS (Sparkline)

Alex — quick pricing framework from our side so you have something concrete going into procurement:

Option A — No-commit Hosted (monthly):
- Baseline unit: $24 / 1M tokens
- Burst allowance: 1.5x baseline concurrency for short windows, billed at 1.25x unit rate for burst tokens beyond baseline
- No guaranteed reserved capacity; automated routing across our pool

Option B — 12-mo Commit (240M/mo anchor):
- Baseline unit: $16 / 1M tokens (annual commitment)
- Guaranteed baseline capacity sized for 99th pct at 160 TPS; additional burst buffer available up to 1.6x with pre-negotiated pricing
- Included quality-preserving quantized variant for non-critical requests (saves ~10-20% on token CPU cost)

Notes & caveats:
- If you cannot accept any model-family fallbacks for user-facing replies, we treat that as 'no-fallback' and capacity planning flips to a higher-cost reserved SKU.
- We can offer a short pilot (30 days) on Option B pricing with an escape clause if traffic grows >35% from anchor.

Next: Mateo and I can build a short mutually agreed MAP (mutual action plan) outlining procurement PO date, pilot start, and SSO/KMS requirements. If you confirm 240M/mo anchor, I will produce a draft SOW + pricing table (PDF) by EOD tomorrow.

-karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

1) We will treat 240M/mo as the working anchor for the first quote.
2) Karthik will circulate the Option A/B PDF (redwood_pricing_options.pdf) + a short MAP tomorrow.
3) You (or procurement) to confirm calendar availability for a 30-min call to sign off on pilot terms (proposed slot Fri 10am PT).
4) Sparkline to share any strict no-fallback endpoints (list of API routes) so we can size reserved capacity where necessary.

Attachments included for reference: sparkline_week1_traffic.csv (from you), sparkline_usage_estimates.csv (our normalized token projection), redwood_pricing_options.pdf (pricing bands).

Thanks — I'll follow up with calendar invites.
